source.title: AdaGrad stepsizes: Sharp convergence over nonconvex landscapes, from any initialization
source.authors: Rachel A. Ward; Xiaoxia Wu; L. Bottou

record.file_problem: Text contains the full paper, including its numerical-experiment discussion and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares AdaGrad-Norm, an adaptive gradient method, with SGD variants on image-classification tasks and reports test accuracy. It does not test the specific adaptive methods or tuning comparisons named in the claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-accuracy outcomes for optimizer comparisons on natural-label datasets. It does not test random-label memorization, width scaling, convolution versus fully connected architectures as a generalization intervention, batch size, dropout, sharpness measures, or memorized-example removal. Exact accuracy values appear only in figures; the prose gives qualitative summaries. Convergence and gradient-norm results are not rows because they do not measure the claim's generalization behavior.
record.test_reason: Section 5.2 compares adaptive AdaGrad variants with SGD using held-out image-classification accuracy while varying the initial stepsize parameter and fixing other parameters. These results bear on V4 despite using different adaptive methods and restricted training recipes.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate but overstates uniform robustness. The authors establish convergence guarantees and report comparable accuracy to tuned SGD in several image settings. They also report divergence for the MNIST CNN at small b0, continued need to tune b0 on ImageNet, and momentum results that depend on b0. The low ImageNet accuracy relative to literature is attributed mainly to the restricted training recipe, rather than an isolated AdaGrad-Norm disadvantage.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates a norm-adaptive stepsize method, including a neural-network implementation that adapts one learning rate per neuron or convolutional channel. It does not reproduce the methods in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The results vary with dataset, model, initialization parameter b0, training epoch, and Batch-Norm configuration. The authors report that AdaGrad-Norm is robust on MNIST and CIFAR-10, while its best-performance range on ImageNet is narrower and suboptimal.

fits_no_version.finding: AdaGrad-Norm has convergence guarantees and generally greater robustness to initial stepsize choices.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adaptive norm-based stepsizes can reduce sensitivity of optimization convergence to initial stepsize choices.

fits_no_version.finding: The best ImageNet test accuracy is approximately ten percentage points below a cited literature benchmark near 76%, under a recipe lacking momentum and the standard decay schedule.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The restricted ImageNet training recipe underperforms standard published recipes; this comparison does not isolate an adaptive-optimizer generalization penalty.

record.problems: Exact image-classification accuracy values are presented in figures without numeric values in the text. The neural-network implementation departs from strict AdaGrad-Norm by adapting per neuron or channel. ImageNet results use no momentum and a constant learning rate, and the authors note that best test accuracy is substantially below literature results.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained. The optimizer comparisons relevant to V4 are summarized qualitatively in the text, but the reported accuracy values are figure-only; the text does not provide exact baseline and intervention values suitable for a row.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Width increases beyond zero training error.
Controlled convolutional versus fully connected generalization comparisons and the role of local connectivity.
Adam and other named adaptive methods, language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching optimizers, and a systematic learning-rate-and-decay-schedule search.
Batch-size interventions under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.

missing.what: Momentum optimizer comparisons omitted from both rows and the specific results declared in rows_left_out: SGD performs better at large b0, while AdaGrad-Norm matches best-stepsize SGD at small b0. Retain qualitative test-accuracy comparisons separately for the two Batch-Norm configurations where supported; exact values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.
missing.locator: Section 5.2, Figure 6 and final paragraph, page 24

record.verdict_notes: There are no extracted rows to repair. Qualitative statements can support verdicts without exact plotted values. Figures 3–5 were already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not repeated as missing. Equality for this adaptive variant qualifies V4's scope; it does not refute the claim that adaptive methods often perform worse.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Widening past the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Comparative generalization of convolutional and fully connected networks under the specified architectural changes.

The paper tests AdaGrad-Norm against SGD variants, but does not test Adam, the cited adaptive optimizers, or the specified learning-rate-and-decay-only tuning comparison. Qualitative optimizer outcomes are described in text, while exact test-accuracy values are figure-only and are not reconstructed as rows.
Large-batch training and its generalization gap under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

relationships.condition: AdaGrad-Norm versus constant-stepsize SGD at well-tuned stepsizes in the image experiments without momentum.
relationships.reason: Section 5.2 explicitly reports almost equal accuracy, qualifying the adaptive-method disadvantage for this neuron/channel-wise variant; based on text because no rows were retained.
relationships.display_finding: Reported nearly equal accuracy between AdaGrad-Norm and constant-step SGD at well-tuned stepsizes remains unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 with momentum 0.9, for initialization b0 above the smoothness constant.
relationships.reason: The Figure 6 discussion explicitly states that momentum SGD performs better than momentum AdaGrad-Norm in this range; based on text, with the corresponding rows missing.
relationships.display_finding: Reported performance favored momentum SGD over momentum AdaGrad-Norm in this initialization range, but the comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 with momentum 0.9, for initialization b0 below the smoothness constant.
relationships.reason: The Figure 6 discussion states that AdaGrad-Norm matches SGD at its best stepsize of 0.1; based on text, with the corresponding rows missing.
relationships.display_finding: Reported AdaGrad-Norm accuracy matching SGD at its best stepsize remains unverified.
